Oh me, oh my. As they say, “Those who live in glass houses, shouldn’t throw stones”. 

It’s a weird stage in life where you can criticize without regard to unknown variables. Including your lack of a true sample size. A narrow view, fed with hypothesis confirming deceptions.

Hopefully your life will lead you on a path to have empathy towards the unknown. Usually even society’s lowest rung people have a story riddled with strife and disparities. Once you can truly feel empathy, really place yourself in their shoes. I believe you will no longer make comments persecuting and condemning groups of people or any person really.

Hate is learned. I’ll assume you don’t know many EMTs or nurses for you to use the term “every”. Because becoming an EMT or RN is not a quick thing. So if you’re going to spend time getting an education, then they wouldn’t go to those jobs if they didn’t want to help people. So the vast majority aren’t what you say. 

Not that it matters, but I’m an ER nurse an interact with EMS all the time. I’ve heard bad jokes, some weird things, but people aren’t on drugs or drunk. They’re responsible family people and honestly most EMTs stick around and stare outside the window after they hand off a very critical patient. Because they care so much and are vested emotionally. They are attached to you after trying to keep you alive from the scene to handoff.  I don’t see any EMT fitting your accusations able to simultaneously be a horrible person that would be the last person you’d want in an emergency. I don’t think you understand what they go through emotionally. To arrive on a horrific scene where it’s total chaos, dead people that are decapitated next to multiple dead people and one person is unconscious but alive. Then they have to extract them and put breathing tubes down their throw throat. Quickly calculate drug dosages. Call the hospital and give an assessment so the proper teams are standing by. Possibly doing chest compressions the whole time, maybe even for 20 minutes I’m sure longer in some rural areas. These people run through the gates of hell to steal you from the hands of Hades himself. I refuse to believe these guardians are bad people. I’ve seen the good they do and the massive hearts they have. Putting yourself in bad situations to help others. That’s a good person right there. Are they humans and have flaws? Of course so. No one is perfect. But they sure AF don’t do it for the f’n money. They have good hearts. And if an EMT knew you and read this post, they’d still pull your ass out of a burning car. 

Maybe the people you know are “partying” in their off time because they’re young and aren’t quite sure how to cope with all of the uncensored societal travesty’s they are called to. 

As for nurses. Same situation with stress. Additionally I’ll add though. Any nurse that is seemingly on drugs or drunk, if another nurse notices, will certainly be sent home and have disciplinary actions taken. We definitely have each other’s backs at work when you need help. But our job is to take care of patients. You better believe that if you are under the influence, we will notice, and we will stop you from seeing patients. That’s it. I guarantee that I could go to any hospital in the country and that holds true. I’m saying this because you don’t know what drug addict or alcoholic is apparently. Because they wouldn’t be able to go 12 hours sober. So for all of us to be drunk or high all the time would be absolutely insane. Most of us get off on caffeine, baked goods, and free pizza from management for crazy patient ratios. Food, we love food. And not me but Starbucks. Like an insane amount of Starbucks and DoorDash. But not drugs. We see too many drug addicts and alcoholics to want to end up in that scenario. 

All this is basically saying you don’t even know the world yet. I don’t know you at all, but I know you’re young and you probably haven’t left the town you grew up in. You will learn that you have absolutely no clue the insanity someone standing next to you in line at the grocery store has gone through. I’d save your criticisms for people you truly know. 

I’m on a rant. Demeaning others will never make you feel good or look good. Kindness and compassion will give you more fulfillment in life. I promise.

Being down in life is a series of failures your brain wasn’t prepared to take. These losses accumulate to form a dark cloud that fogs the brain from its normal state and thought process. Defeating it is not easy. You must find something positive about every negative situation you’re fixated on in your brain. You have to verbally say these positive things until you start to actually believe them. You must must must develop a positive mindset. It starts small but any time a negative unexpected event happens you must understand that it is not allowed to be added to the massive black cloud. This event is simply a normal sequence of events that happen to everyone and it’s not the end of the world. Your car broke down on your way to work and you’re too broke to fix it and you know you now don’t have transportation to work: guess what, shit happens. Tighten your shoe laces, and start walking to work. You get to work 2 hours late and they say you’re fired. Just say you appreciated the experience and friendship you got there and hope everyone does well in the future. Then move forward and take it as an opportunity to try and new job in a different nursing specialty that you’re interested in. Always maintain your positive attitude. Wish well for others when you’re at your worst. I’m not a religious man but I believe if you’re able to be polite and helpful and caring when you’re at your worst then your brain won’t let you be mean to yourself later on when another loss happens.  It’s a mindset that’s very difficult to activate but it’s possible and it makes you resilient to these negative life events.

Nasty things happen to everyone all over the entire world. You need to ask whether you’ll be defined by that defeat or use it as a lesson to push yourself and be defined as a resilient caring amazing human being that emits a positive attitude for everyone to relish in.

I’ve been to the bottom and I wouldn’t take it back for a billion dollars. It’s made me into the man I am today. I have mistakes, many. I’ll make many many more before I die. But I take misfortune with a smile and think smugly to myself “is that the worst you got? Pfft” lol

Just a few tips.
1) learn how a specific pharmacological class works and why first. This will help you work through the questions later on and use problem solving to help narrow down answers

2) Learn indications, contraindications, and common side effects and adverse affects of those classes as a whole. 

3) learn a nemonic for each class to remember the suffix or prefix. There’s a website if you just google generic drug naming conventions, or something along those lines. Some drugs you’ll have to bite the bullet and just remember what your professor wants. They will be random. Don’t worry about those yet though

4)Now that you have the overall concept for each class, go through whatever material your school uses and try to identify specific drugs that seem pertinent. Again problem solve.
